subject: [PATCH] mm/khugepaged: don't map folios that are not uptodate in MADV_COLLAPSE

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested rejecting the MADV_COLLAPSE operation and logging a warning when folios are not uptodate, instead of just asserting it
reviews.raw_body:
I think so. But looking at these hard-to-trigger but in the end very nasty
problems, should we actually reject the operation and do a pr_warn_once() or
something?

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing David's feedback that the patch should assert whether a folio is uptodate in set_pte_range() and do_set_pmd(). The author agrees that rejecting the mapping is better than asserting, and instead proposes to add a function file_folio_not_uptodate() that checks if a folio is uptodate. This function will be called from finish_fault(), do_set_pmd(), and other places where it's necessary. The author provides a patch with compile-tested changes.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer requested that the suggested assertion be sent as a proper patch, indicating agreement with the proposed change to catch potential issues.
reviews.raw_body:
Can you send that as a proper patch? I think this is the right thing to do to
catch more of these things if they ever pop up in a better way.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Pedro Falcato
reviews.summary: Reviewer Pedro Falcato expressed concerns about the fragility of page table manipulation APIs and usage in the kernel, specifically highlighting instances where it's possible to perform operations without holding necessary locks or with incorrect folio states. He suggested adding basic assertions (initially VM_WARN_ON_ONCE) to prevent such issues.
reviews.raw_body:
Yes. FWIW, this is something that's been going through my mind. Our page table
manipulation APIs (and usage) are way too fragile and allow you to do the
most insane things without ever realizing it (e.g you can clear a pte, set
over a PTE, get-and-clear and discard the result, and do all of the above with
no locks held, set a pte for a folio that's not uptodate, set a pte for a folio
for which you don't have the lock, etc).

Some basic assertions (even if there's no easy way to back down from those)
would be nice, or ideally yes a rejection.

I would just add that these very much should be VM_WARN_ON_ONCE instead of
pr_warn_once(). pr_warn_once() will (AIUI) not be caught by fuzzers, at least
not as easily.

Also, if they're inexpensive enough, we might want to upgrade them to full
WARN_ON_ONCE().

-- 
Pedro

2026-11-06.patch_summary: This patch prevents the khugepaged from mapping folios that are not up-to-date when using MADV_COLLAPSE, addressing a previously overlooked issue where other callers checked for up-to-dateness but khugepaged did not. The fix involves adding an assertion to ensure that the folio is up-to-date before attempting to map it. This change ensures consistency in handling up-to-dateness across different mapping scenarios.
